## This game

A new game. You play Black, so you move first.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I’ll read the last two reviews, retain the 20k opponent, and play game 195 to completion. I’ll preserve the raw boards and record the lessons for the next session.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.

const review=`# Game 195: Black vs 20k — W+R

Played 2026-10-07. Chinese area scoring, komi7, simple ko.
Black resigned after White56 A6; closing board confirms W+R, next57.
Physical captures Black1/White0. No ko, invalid Go move or passes.

Game52 discrepancy and99/106 evidence limits remain separate.

## Exact moves

${v.moves.map(m=>m.number+" "+(m.color==="X"?"B":"W")+" "+m.move).join(", ")}.

## Opening count: a fragile outline with unfinished middle boundaries

After10, before Black11 D3, saved OPEN46:
ABCDE rows1-9 except White E6 =44, plus F1/F2 =2.
Disjoint and explicitly unsecured, with no two-eye proof.
Only one prospective point above Black's45 winning threshold.
The reference included unbuilt middle boundaries and future lower-right extension, so it was a development target rather than established ownership.

C3/C7/E7 began separately. D7 at7 ACTUALLY joined C7/E7.
E3 at9 began separately; D3 at11 ACTUALLY joined it to C3.
D5 at13 was separate and White14 D4 occupied the junction below it.
C4 at15 joined the lower chain; White16 D6 cut the upper junction.
C5 at17 ACTUALLY joined D5 to the lower chain.
White18 C6 then occupied the remaining direct upper/lower junction.
The two left bases remained physically separate through resignation.

Black19 F8 began separately; White20 B6 expanded the left cut.
E8 at21 ACTUALLY joined F8 to E7/main.
White22 B7 and Black23 B8 bounded the upper left; B8 was initially separate.
White24 E2 undercut the lower outline.
D2 at25 joined D3 and protected the lower boundary.
C8 at33 ACTUALLY joined B8 to C7/main.
White34 G8 capped the intended top extension.
The upper group ended with seven stones and one open, undivided upper region; no completed two-eye divider was played.
No claim is made that a different opening or timing forced a win.

## Left invasion and an insufficient lower room

White26 A4 began separately.
B4/B3 at27/29 joined the lower chain and bounded the invader from the right.
White28 A3 and30 A5 extended it along the edge.
A6 was still an open route to White B6; no containment or capture proof existed.
D1 at31 joined D2 and protected the bottom endpoint, but did not complete two eyes.

Black51 A2 began SEPARATELY with A1/B2 liberties.
White52 B1 invaded the unfinished lower room with A1/B2/C1 liberties.
B2 at53 ACTUALLY joined A2 to B3/main and removed B2 from that invader.
White54 C1 joined B1; the pair then had A1/C2.
These were shared liberties, not two Black eyes.

Black55 B5 joined B4/C5 and put White A3/A4/A5 soleA6.
The placed attacker was supported by the lower main; the separate right J7 was already in atari and remained so.
White56 A6 ACTUALLY joined the three-stone invader to B6/White's central chain.
This saved the attacked chain. It was not an ignored atari and no left capture occurred.

Final lower thirteen Black stones had A1/C2/E1/E5 liberties.
E1 and E5 border the broad White chain. A1/C2 border the separate White B1/C1 pair.
None is currently a completed true eye.
Manually occupying one of A1/C2 and subsequently capturing B1/C1 at the other would reopen adjacent B1/C1 as ONE two-point room.
That local capture does not supply two independent eyes.
It does not prove every possible continuation forced: resignation was a practical assessment of lost width and incomplete life, not a searched proof of death.

## Right recovery: other-chain capture rescue and vulnerable shared eye

H4 at35 began a separate replacement base.
White36 H5 capped above; H3 at37 joined H4, and White38 H2 undercut below.
G3/G4/G5 at39/41/43 continuously joined the right chain.
White40 G2 connected H2 to F2/main.
White42 F5 joined its upper and lower central chains; White44 G6 closed the G5 escape.
The five right stones then had ONLY J3/J4, neither an eye.
The second-eye audit failed before continued recovery.

Black45 H6 began SEPARATELY with H7/J6 liberties and put isolated White H5 soleJ5.
This was a supported-by-two-own-liberties atari.
All other friendly chains were checked at that moment; the right five had two liberties, not atari.
White46 J3 ignored H5's atari but put the DIFFERENT right five soleJ4.

Black47 J5 LEGALLY captured White H5 one.
J5 began SEPARATELY with reopened H5, J4 and J6 liberties.
The capture REOPENED H5 for BOTH the right five and separate H6.
Thus the right five's sole-J4 atari dissolved without Black playing J4.
This is an actual other-chain capture rescue, not an orthogonal join.
Physical capture totals became Black1/White0 and remained there.

White48 H7 capped H6.
Black49 J7 began SEPARATELY with J6/J8 liberties.
J6 then had only Black boundary stones H6/J5/J7, but its boundary was conditional on the isolated J7 surviving.
White50 J8 put J7 soleJ6.
J6 was therefore not an unconditional shared eye:
a White entry at J6 can capture J7 while H6 and J5 retain H5.
The capture opens J7 for the entering White stone. Friendly geometric borders alone do not establish a true eye.

J6 would actually join H6/J5/J7, but after that connection the right side would still rely on H5 and enemy-bordered J4.
White J4 has access to its J3 stone, which retains J2.
Do not call J4 a second eye, or count a connection as a whole-base life proof.
H5 also remained conditional on separate boundary groups surviving; no unconditional two-eye claim is justified.
No further right move was submitted. J7 remained in atari at resignation.

## Lessons to use immediately
1. Count prospective area early, especially after about 10-16 moves. With all 81 points assigned, Black needs at least 45 for a win with 7 komi; 44-37 is a draw. If there is neutral area, compare actual totals instead.
2. Center influence must yield territory, an attack, or access to a viable invasion. Game 1 built a narrow central chain while White took both sides.
3. Check two eyes for every major group before treating it as safe. Connected stones and many present liberties are not proof of life. Preserve eye space and a base before filling internal points.
4. In capture reading, rebuild the position after each capture. Captured stones open liberties for adjacent enemy groups. The D8/E9 sacrifice in game 1 overlooked this.
5. Ko eyes are not unconditional eyes. Game 1's lower D2 and upper E8 spaces depended on vulnerable isolated Black stones. Owning two such ko positions does not by itself guarantee double-ko life.
6. Do not repeat the complete opening E5 C5 E3 D7 F7 G5 G6 H6 G7 G3 without reconsidering its territorial consequences. E5 itself was not shown to be wrong.
